proved: A completed adversarial job remains transient until an explicit save action names the exact current project research revision and human attribution; the archive separately retains the exact source document revision and research revision at save.

The saved canonical archive includes the original question, exact selected source excerpts, validated public result, compute-matched baselines, call ledger, native authorization metadata, and content-free provider provenance.

Every archive read rechecks exact fields, size, canonical SHA-256, request validity, reconstructed deterministic plan, exact source ordering, run semantics, call graph coverage, call-ledger accounting, provider/model/task/timeout/output-limit routing, provider usage, and provider-run semantic validity.
Archive records are limited to 32 MiB each and 2,000 per project; decision history is limited to 20,000 bounded events.
Peer-namespaced Yjs keys allow identical disconnected archives to converge while preserving same-run different-content collisions for fail-closed inspection.

Human accepted/rejected decisions are separate immutable exact-parent events bound to the archive SHA-256 and exact project revision; exact domain retries are idempotent and concurrent branches remain conflicted instead of selecting a timestamp winner.
Saving and deciding use the existing provider-neutral project discussions collection, require no persisted Zustand save-shape migration, and never read or mutate the Lexical editor root.
Routine research inspection returns bounded IDs, hashes, counts, attribution metadata, decision state, and integrity issues while omitting question, source, result, and decision-note bodies.

MCP exposes explicit save_adversarial_review and decide_adversarial_review tools. The save tool description discloses that full research content becomes shared project content and may synchronize through Drive.

Headless tests reject stale saves, extra provider payload fields, substituted provider routes, substituted usage, malformed nested archives, mismatched decision/archive hashes, reused identities, same-run archive conflicts, and concurrent decision branches.
The embedded MCP advertises 34 strict semantic tools over protocol 2025-11-25 with clean stdio.
